books.title: 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
books.description:
A business and self-help book written by Stephen Covey.
It presents a principle-centered approach for solving personal and professional problems.
Through seven foundational habits, it teaches readers how to cultivate effectiveness and leadership.
It remains one of the most influential guidance books for personal development and growth.

books.title: Atomic Habits
books.description:
An easy & proven way to build good habits & break bad ones.
Written by James Clear, the book focuses on small behavioral shifts that compound into remarkable results.
It outlines practical strategies based on biology, psychology, and neuroscience to reshape daily routines.
Readers discover how to design environments that make success automatic and sustainable over time.

A dystopian social science fiction novel and cautionary tale.
It depicts a totalitarian regime led by Big Brother that practices extreme surveillance and mind control.
The protagonist, Winston Smith, attempts to rebel against the oppressive party and rediscover individual freedom.
It stands as a timeless masterpiece warning against the dangers of authoritarianism and manipulation of truth.

books.title: Brave New World
books.description:
A dystopian novel by English author Aldous Huxley.
It envisions a futuristic society driven by technological advancements, genetic engineering, and psychological conditioning.
Citizens are kept perpetually pacified through artificial happiness and the suppression of deep emotion.
The narrative challenges readers to consider the true cost of convenience, stability, and loss of individuality.

books.title: The Catcher in the Rye
books.description:
A story about teenage angst and alienation.
It follows the iconic protagonist Holden Caulfield as he wanders through New York City after being expelled.
Through Holden's cynical yet vulnerable voice, the book explores themes of innocence, grief, and identity.
It has resonated with generations of readers navigating the complex transition from childhood to adulthood.

books.title: Deep Work
books.description:
Rules for focused success in a distracted world.
Cal Newport argues that professional activities performed in distraction-free concentration are becoming increasingly rare and valuable.
He provides a rigorous framework and actionable training regimen to upgrade cognitive capacity and eliminate shallow tasks.
The book demonstrates how mastering this skill leads to superior results in less time.

books.title: The Four Agreements
books.description:
A practical guide to personal freedom based on Toltec wisdom.
Don Miguel Ruiz reveals the source of self-limiting beliefs that rob people of joy and create needless suffering.
It outlines four simple yet powerful rules: be impeccable with your word, don't take anything personally, don't make assumptions, and always do your best.
Adopting these principles helps transform perspective and foster inner peace.

books.title: The Great Gatsby
books.description:
A 1925 novel by American writer F. Scott Fitzgerald.
Set in the Jazz Age on Long Island, it follows the enigmatic millionaire Jay Gatsby and his obsession with Daisy Buchanan.
Through lush prose, it critiques the American Dream against a backdrop of wealth, class division, and moral decay.
It remains a cornerstone of American literature and cultural critique.

books.title: Homo Deus
books.description:
A brief history of tomorrow by Yuval Noah Harari.
It explores the grand projects facing humanity in the 21st century, shifting from overcoming famine and plague to pursuing immortality and happiness.
The book investigates how dataism and artificial intelligence might eventually supersede human agency.
It offers a provocative look at the potential trajectories of evolution and civilization.

books.title: Sapiens
books.description:
A brief history of humankind.
Yuval Noah Harari surveys the history of our species from the Stone Age up to the modern technological era.
It highlights how cognitive, agricultural, and scientific revolutions shaped societies through shared myths and cooperation.
The text connects biology and history to explain how Homo sapiens came to dominate planet Earth.

books.title: The Intelligent Investor
books.description:
The definitive book on value investing.
Benjamin Graham outlines core strategies to protect portfolios from substantial error and develop long-term financial discipline.
It teaches investors how to analyze market fluctuations and focus on the intrinsic value of businesses.
Widely praised by legendary figures like Warren Buffett, it remains an indispensable financial guide.

books.title: The Lean Startup
books.description:
How constant innovation creates radically successful businesses.
Eric Ries introduces a methodology that favors validated learning, rapid experimentation, and iterative product releases.
It helps entrepreneurs test visions continuously and adapt before large-scale capital investments are made.
The approach revolutionizes how startups are built and managed in fast-changing markets.

books.title: The Power of Habit
books.description:
Why we do what we do in life and business.
Charles Duhigg explores the neurological loop underlying habit formation consisting of cue, routine, and reward.
Through engaging case studies, he explains how individuals, companies, and organizations transform their operations.
It empowers readers to harness habit loops to achieve lasting personal and collective change.

books.title: Rich Dad Poor Dad
books.description:
What the rich teach their kids about money.
Robert Kiyosaki contrasts the financial mindsets and philosophies of his biological father with his rich surrogate father.
It challenges conventional wisdom regarding jobs, assets, liabilities, and formal financial education.
The book encourages readers to build asset columns that generate passive income and financial freedom.

books.title: The Alchemist
books.description:
A magical novel about following your dream.
It tells the mystical story of Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy who journeys toward Egypt in search of hidden treasure.
Along the way, he learns to listen to his heart and understand the language of the universe.
It has inspired millions of readers worldwide to pursue their personal destinies.

books.title: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
books.description:
A counterintuitive approach to living a good life.
Mark Manson argues that embracing limitations, flaws, and adversities leads to genuine strength and resilience.
Instead of chasing constant positivity, readers learn to choose what truly matters to them.
It delivers refreshing, blunt advice on finding meaning through personal responsibility.

books.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
books.description:
Explores the two systems that drive the way we think.
Daniel Kahneman details System 1, which is fast and emotional, versus System 2, which is slower and more logical.
It highlights cognitive biases, heuristics, and mental shortcuts that affect decision-making in everyday life.
The groundbreaking work bridges behavioral economics and cognitive psychology.

books.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
books.description:
Pulitzer Prize-winning novel by Harper Lee.
Set in the American South, it addresses deeply rooted racial injustice and moral growth through young Scout Finch's eyes.
Her father, Atticus Finch, defends a falsely accused Black man, demonstrating profound integrity.
It stands as a monumental pillar of classic American fiction and social conscience.

books.title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
books.description:
One of the best-selling self-help books of all time.
Dale Carnegie provides timeless fundamental techniques for handling people and improving interpersonal communication.
It emphasizes empathy, appreciation, and genuine interest in others to build lasting relationships.
The practical principles continue to guide professional success and social harmony.

books.title: Palace Walk
books.description:
The first novel of the famous Cairo Trilogy by Naguib Mahfouz.
It captures family life in Cairo during the politically turbulent era leading up to the 1919 revolution.
Centered around the patriarchal figure Al-Sayyid Ahmad, it portrays strict domestic traditions alongside shifting national identities.
It is widely celebrated as a masterpiece of modern Arabic literature.

books.title: Diary of a Country Prosecutor
books.description:
Diary of a Country Prosecutor by Tawfiq el-Hakim.
It reflects the harrowing experiences and bureaucratic hurdles faced by a young official working in rural Egypt.
Through sharp irony and realism, it critiques the disconnect between formal law and impoverished village realities.
The narrative remains a foundational text in Egyptian narrative fiction.

books.title: The Blue Elephant
books.description:
A psychological thriller novel by Ahmed Mourad.
It follows a troubled psychiatrist who encounters a mysterious criminal case involving a former close friend.
Blending mental illness, ancient Egyptian symbolism, and suspense, the plot keeps readers guessing.
It became a major contemporary bestseller adapted successfully into cinema.

books.title: God's World
books.description:
A famous collection of short stories by Youssef Idries.
It captures the social struggles, emotional depths, and daily realities of ordinary Egyptian people.
Idries masterfully uses colloquial realism to portray human dignity under difficult socioeconomic conditions.
The anthology highlights his exceptional contribution to Arab short story writing.

books.title: Memory in the Flesh
books.description:
A prominent Arabic novel by Ahlam Mosteghanemi.
It weaves a poetic narrative of love, revolution, and artistic expression across Algeria and France.
The story connects a wounded painter with the daughter of his fallen revolutionary mentor.
It won high acclaim for its lyrical prose and profound emotional resonance.

books.title: Granada
books.description:
A historical novel trilogy by Radwa Ashour.
It chronicles the lives of an Andalusian family following the fall of Granada in 1492.
The trilogy beautifully depicts cultural preservation, persecution, and resilience under Spanish rule.
It stands as a monumental achievement in modern historical fiction.

books.title: The Yacoubian Building
books.description:
A bestselling novel detailing life in downtown Cairo by Alaa El Aswany.
It portrays an eclectic cast of residents inside a single apartment building, reflecting broader societal shifts.
The characters expose corruption, political oppression, religious extremism, and social inequality.
It became an international literary phenomenon translated into numerous languages.

books.title: Woman at Point Zero
books.description:
A powerful biographical novel by Nawal El Saadawi.
It recounts the life of Firdaus, a female prisoner awaiting execution who refuses to speak until her final hours.
Through her harrowing testimony, the book exposes systemic oppression and patriarchy in Egyptian society.
It remains a classic text of international feminist literature.

books.title: House of Jasmine
books.description:
An acclaimed novel by Ibrahim Abdel Meguid.
It captures the atmospheric historical texture and human interactions within Alexandria's diverse communities.
The narrative explores memory, identity, and political upheaval across shifting eras.
Abdel Meguid's lyrical style highlights the cultural richness of Egyptian coastal life.

books.title: Legend of the Other World
books.description:
Part of the famous metaphysical and horror series by Ahmed Khaled Tawfik.
It follows supernatural investigator Refaat Ismail as he encounters terrifying paranormal phenomena.
The story blends science fiction, folklore, and dark mystery in signature engaging fashion.
It captivated generations of young Arab readers interested in speculative fiction.

books.title: Utopia
books.description:
A dystopian sci-fi novel set in future Egypt by Ahmed Khaled Tawfik.
It depicts an isolated gated community for the ultra-rich walled off from an impoverished, lawless wasteland.
The plot escalates when a bored resident ventures outside for a dangerous thrill.
It serves as a stark social critique of extreme class disparity.

books.title: Clean Code
books.description:
A handbook of agile software craftsmanship by Robert C. Martin.
It teaches developers how to write code that is readable, maintainable, and extensible.
The book uses numerous examples to illustrate good versus bad programming practices.
It is widely regarded as essential reading for professional software engineers.

books.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
books.description:
The definitive textbook on artificial intelligence by Stuart Russell and Peter Norvig.
It offers comprehensive coverage of modern AI techniques, search algorithms, and neural networks.
The text is standard curriculum across universities worldwide for computer science students.
It explores both theoretical foundations and practical implementations of intelligent agents.

books.title: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow
books.description:
Concepts, tools, and techniques to build intelligent systems by Aurélien Géron.
It provides practical coding examples using popular Python libraries for deep learning.
Readers learn how to train models for computer vision, natural language processing, and regression.
It bridges theoretical machine learning concepts with real-world application building.

books.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
books.description:
Your journey to mastery in software development.
It offers practical advice on career growth, code debugging, and architectural design.
The authors share timeless tips to avoid technical debt and boost productivity.
It is a staple reference for developers aiming for engineering excellence.

books.title: Deep Learning
books.description:
An MIT Press textbook on deep learning fundamentals by Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, and Aaron Courville.
It covers mathematical prerequisites, deep feedforward networks, and optimization techniques.
The book serves as an authoritative reference for researchers and advanced practitioners.
It details the core mechanics driving modern artificial intelligence breakthroughs.

books.title: Learning Python
books.description:
Comprehensive introduction to the Python programming language.
It guides readers through core syntax, data structures, and object-oriented programming.
The book provides clear explanations and code exercises suitable for all skill levels.
It remains a trusted guide for mastering Python development fundamentals.

books.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
books.description:
The big ideas behind reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems by Martin Kleppmann.
It explores trade-offs in database architectures, streaming systems, and batch processing.
Engineers learn how to build robust distributed systems capable of handling massive data loads.
It is widely celebrated as the best practical guide to backend system design.

books.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: The Biography
books.description:
An in-depth biography covering the relentless ambition, rivalries, and records of Cristiano Ronaldo.
Guillem Balagué traces his incredible rise from Madeira to global football icon.
It highlights his unmatched work ethic, dedication, and competitive drive.
Fans gain fascinating insights into the person behind the legendary celebrations.

books.title: Inverting the Pyramid: The History of Football Tactics
books.description:
The definitive history of football tactics, exploring how the greatest minds shaped the beautiful game.
Jonathan Wilson tracks tactical evolution from Victorian formations to modern pressing systems.
It explains the philosophy behind legendary managers and winning teams.
An essential read for anyone passionate about football analysis.

books.title: Ronaldo: The Rise of a Winner
books.description:
The inspiring biography of Cristiano Ronaldo, tracing his journey from Madeira to global superstardom.
Luca Caioli examines the pivotal moments that defined his career across Manchester United and Real Madrid.
It underscores the discipline required to maintain peak athletic performance.
A compelling tribute to a footballing legend.

books.title: State of Play: The Secret Economy of Modern Football
books.description:
An eye-opening look into the multi-billion dollar business and hidden mechanics of modern professional football.
Miguel Delaney investigates transfers, club ownership, and financial regulations.
It exposes the commercial pressures shaping the sport today.
Readers discover the economic forces behind favorite clubs.

books.title: The Ball is Round: A Global History of Football
books.coverUrl: /images/The Ball is Round A Global Histo.jpg
books.description:
A comprehensive and magisterial history of how football conquered the world.
David Goldblatt explores the social, cultural, and political dimensions of the sport.
It covers legendary matches, players, and global tournaments across continents.
A definitive encyclopedia for true football historians.

books.title: You Can Heal Your Life
books.description:
A classic self-help guide on how our beliefs and thoughts can contribute to emotional and physical well-being by Louise Hay.
It promotes positive affirmations and self-love to overcome inner obstacles.
The book has empowered millions to transform their mental outlook and health.
An influential text in the personal growth movement.

books.title: Ancient Egypt (The Classical Encyclopedia)
books.description:
A comprehensive foundational reference for the history of Pharaonic civilization, its customs, and beliefs by a pioneering Egyptian Egyptologist.
Selim Hassan details archaeological findings across temples and royal tombs.
It provides unmatched scholarly depth on ancient Egyptian society.
An essential masterpiece for Egyptology enthusiasts.

books.title: The Rise and Fall of Ancient Egypt
books.description:
An insightful historical analysis chronicling the Pharaohs from the dawn of unification to the empire's fall, highlighting politics and power struggles.
Toby Wilkinson brings ancient history to life with engaging narrative flair.
It examines the triumphs and tragedies of royal dynasties.
A captivating read on ancient civilization dynamics.

books.title: Hatshepsut: The Female Pharaoh
books.description:
A fascinating historical biography exploring one of ancient Egypt's greatest female rulers, under whom trade and arts deeply flourished.
Christian Desroches Noblecourt details her rise to power and architectural achievements.
It celebrates her enduring legacy along the Nile.
A brilliant tribute to New Kingdom history.
